assessment: This important study addresses the question of how pathogen reservoirs can play a role in the emergence of new virulences, using beets and Uromyces beticola as a pathosystem. The authors find convincing evidence for higher signals of diversity and differentiation in effector genes and significant differences in reproductive rates between two pathogen populations that occur either on wild or on wild and domesticated beets. These findings have the potential for developing approaches that reduce the evolution of pathogen resistance in crops.
